newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks roll to 18th record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks roll to 18th record close.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index on Friday posted its 18th record close this year and second straight this week, aided by New York's spectacular rally and declining interest rate concerns.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 35 points to a new high of 6550.61.
"We basically followed New York," Maison Placements Canada trader Rolie Bradley said.

Bradley added that the gain was also fueled by the rally in the Canadian fixed-income market. The Canadian 30-year benchmark bond yield on Thursday dropped below its U.S. counterpart for the first time ever.
Canada's 30-year yielded 6.72 percent, while the U.S. finished at 6.73 percent on Friday.
Investors snapped up interest-sensitive issues such as utilities and pipelines, Bradley said.

Market players also cheered an unexpectedly soft U.S. producer price index for May, which was interpreted as lowering the chances that the Federal Reserve would raise short-term rates at its July 1-2 meeting.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors closed higher, led by media, utilities, retail and oils. The four weaker groups included golds and consumer products.
Trading was active at 97.9 million shares worth C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion).
Among hot stocks, vehicle parts market Magna International Inc. rose 2.45 to 83.75 in heavy turnover, climbing for the third straight day since reporting record sales and profit earlier in the week.
Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc. rose 0.60 to 40.40 in brisk trading.

Canada's largest publicly traded company gained after its telephone unit Bell Canada asked the national regulator, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, to hike local telephone rates.
